title: PowerShell opens LSASS with full-access rights on scranton (credential dumping access)
rationale: All six findings describe the same action: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976) on scranton.dmevals.local opening lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff (PROCESS_VM_READ/PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS) at 2020-05-02T03:05:16Z, plus the wsmprovhost.exe LSASS access on nashua. This is the canonical LSASS memory access pattern for credential extraction, best fitting T1003.001 (LSASS Memory). F34/F37/F48 note the absence of authentication-process modification artifacts, so T1556/T1555.004 are not the best fit.

title: WebDAV forced authentication via davclnt DavSetCookie to 192.168.0.4
rationale: The WebClient service spawning rundll32 davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie pointed at attacker host 192.168.0.4 is the canonical forced-authentication mechanism causing the victim to authenticate and leak NTLM credentials, matching T1187.

title: accesschk.exe creates 'passwordsDB' file on scranton
rationale: Both findings describe accesschk.exe (invoked by pbeesly) writing a file named 'passwordsDB' to disk, indicating credential material collected into a file — unsecured credentials in files (T1552.001).

title: PsExec64 launched on NASHUA with hardcoded plaintext credentials
rationale: PsExec64 invoked with cleartext -u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by on the command line is credential material embedded in a command line, matching unsecured credentials (T1552.001).

title: PowerShell Get-PrivateKeys exports LocalMachine certificates with private keys to .pfx
rationale: Both findings describe the same Get-PrivateKeys script (readme.ps1) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and calling Export-PfxCertificate to write private keys to .pfx files protected by hardcoded password 'saribas' — direct private-key theft, matching T1552.004.

title: PowerShell exports private-key .pfx to Downloads on scranton
rationale: powershell.exe writing coyn5igj.3io.pfx to the user's Downloads is credential material exported to disk; the finding is tagged as credentials from password stores (T1555.003).

title: SMB/WinRM/RPC traffic from spoofed 10.0.1.4 to NASHUA with Kerberos cifs/NASHUA tickets
rationale: Spoofed-source SMB/WinRM/RPC traffic to NASHUA with Kerberos TGS requests for cifs/NASHUA and HTTP/NASHUA immediately after MAC takeover is consistent with name-resolution poisoning/SMB relay credential capture, matching T1557.001.

title: ARP cache poisoning / AiTM positioning on 10.0.1.0/24
rationale: Both findings describe MAC fc:bd:67:e1:a9:c1 claiming IP 10.0.1.4 alongside the legitimate MAC, redirecting 10.0.1.4<->10.0.1.6 flows — the signature of ARP cache poisoning, matching T1557.002.

title: Outbound SMB/WebDAV probing to 192.168.0.4 and SMB to 10.0.1.6 from scranton
rationale: Rejected SMB connections to 192.168.0.4 and large SMB transfers to 10.0.1.6 are network connection/remote-service activity, not credential access.

title: PowerShell compiles in-memory C# credential tooling via csc.exe on scranton
rationale: csc.exe compiling C# source into DLLs in random temp folders is in-memory tooling compilation (execution), not credential access itself.

title: Invoke-Exfil script with hardcoded credentials and WebDAV exfiltration
rationale: The Invoke-Exfil script compresses the Downloads folder and copies it to a WebDAV share at 192.168.0.4; this is collection and exfiltration over web service, not credential access.

title: Steganographic PowerShell loader (monkey.png) executed hidden with execution-policy bypass
rationale: control.exe spawning PowerShell with -noni -noexit -ep bypass -window hidden to decode and IEX a payload from monkey.png is execution/defense-evasion (PowerShell execution), not credential access itself.

title: Password-protected RAR archive created then wiped with sdelete on NASHUA
rationale: Rar.exe creating a password-protected archive of working.zip followed by sdelete64.exe secure deletion is local data staging and indicator removal, not credential access.

title: Suspicious .scr payload in C:\ProgramData\victim launched by explorer on scranton
rationale: The .scr binary launched by explorer.exe is the steganographic-payload staging binary — user execution of a malicious file, not credential access.

title: hostui.exe spawned by PowerShell on scranton
rationale: hostui.exe spawned by PowerShell is a known UAC-bypass binary invocation (privilege escalation/defense evasion), not credential access.

title: sdclt.exe spawned by cmd on scranton
rationale: sdclt.exe spawned by cmd.exe is a known UAC-bypass binary invocation (privilege escalation/defense evasion), not credential access.

title: python.exe executed on NASHUA via PsExec service under pbeesly
rationale: python.exe spawned by PSEXESVC.exe on NASHUA is remote execution via PsExec service (lateral movement), not credential access.
